evidence.note: Agent forms spec-driven hypotheses about classification bugs (train/test sampling; re-creating RandomState(42) per experiment) and patches — targeted, not random, but triggered by re-reading the spec rather than any observed score divergence.

Flags a pair-classification negation/threshold convention as suspect (25) but then rationalizes it away as 'numerically equivalent, no urgent patch needed' (53) without any numerical test — anchor-3-style talking itself out of a real distinction.

Final validation is structural only (keys/numeric/finite). No comparison of computed main_scores against the mteb leaderboard or spec values ever occurs, so no divergence is ever detected or diagnosed via numbers.
Extensive polling of runs verifies only that tasks execute and pass structural checks; the loop never closes on numerical correctness, so the hypothesize-test-correct cycle is incomplete.

reasoning: The agent forms plausible, specific protocol hypotheses and makes targeted patches (shuffle re-creation, classification sampling), which is above the random-tweak level 3, but it never grounds corrections in an observed score divergence — no leaderboard/spec numerical cross-check ever happens, so it cannot trace a mismatch to a root cause and re-verify (falling short of level 5). It also rationalizes away a genuine convention distinction (step 53) without testing. This places it just above 3: engaged, spec-aware hypothesizing, but no numerically-grounded diagnose-fix-reconfirm loop.
